Sidney Lumet’s 12 Angry Men (1957) is one of the greatest courtroom dramas ever made, even though almost the entire film takes place inside a single jury room.

The story follows twelve jurors deciding the fate of a young man accused of murder. Eleven believe he’s guilty, but one man, played brilliantly by Henry Fonda, isn’t so sure.

One of the most fascinating details is how Lumet used the camera to build tension. As the film progresses, the camera gradually moves closer to the actors and shifts to lower angles, making the room feel smaller and more claustrophobic.

It was Sidney Lumet’s feature directorial debut, and he managed to create an incredibly gripping film with almost no action, no elaborate sets, and mostly just twelve men arguing around a table.

Nearly 70 years later, 12 Angry Men remains one of the finest examples of how powerful great writing, acting, and directing can be.
